sources.searcher_note: ERCOT's first Firm Fuel Supply Service award after Uri: 2,940.5 MW procured, 18 of 19 units on fuel oil. Different measure from the lead: MW paid to hold backup fuel, not total gas capacity able to switch to oil; no share or before/after comparison.

sources.quote: dual-fuel capable generation units with on-site alternative fuel storage, and generators that own and control the pipeline to a storage facility
sources.searcher_note: Texas PUC limited the first phase of the post-Uri firm-fuel product to dual-fuel units with on-site fuel storage. Policy context; no count or share of dual-fuel gas capacity.

sources.quote: The most common mode of fuel switching in the United States is from natural gas to petroleum liquids, at almost 132 GW of capacity.
sources.searcher_note: National EIA-860 fuel-switching pattern; regional detail for Florida, New England, New York only. Nothing on Texas, ERCOT, SPP or MISO.

notes: No source found reporting the share of ERCOT gas capacity able to switch to oil, before or after Uri (4.9% to 5.5-6.0%), or the SPP (17.2% to 13.6%) and MISO (18.5% to 17.8%) figures. Closest coverage is ERCOT's Firm Fuel Supply Service: about 2,940 MW procured for winter 2022-23, nearly all fuel-oil backup. That is a different measure (paid backup-fuel MW, not EIA-860 switch-capable capacity). The ERCOT FFSS program page lists offer data for 2024-25 through 2026-27 in spreadsheets not read. The FERC/NERC Uri report came up in search, but no dual-fuel share was found in the summaries fetched. No coverage dated after 2026-06-30 on this measure found. No source found that disagrees.
